1. # **Introduction**

   1. ## ***Purpose*** 

This document is the Software Requirements Specification (SRS) for the Intelligent Research & IP System (IRIS) — a ground-up reimplementation of the Intellectual Property Asset Management System at Cebu Institute of Technology – University (CIT-U). The predecessor system, IPAMS v2.0, was evaluated during the project's inception phase and found to be architecturally irreparable for the required scale, feature scope, and compliance obligations. IRIS does not modify or extend the IPAMS v2.0 codebase; it replaces it entirely with a redesigned backend, a restructured database schema, and a new frontend, while preserving continuity of institutional data and workflows.

This SRS provides a complete and unambiguous description of the functional requirements, non-functional requirements, external interfaces, and system constraints governing IRIS. It shall serve as the authoritative specification for all design, implementation, and testing decisions, and as the contractual baseline between the development team and institutional stakeholders. Any change to the system's behavior or scope shall require a corresponding revision to this document, recorded in the Change History table.

The intended audience of this SRS includes:

* **Research and Development Coordinating Office (RDCO) Directors —** to verify that the system enforces the correct institutional approval workflow and provides the required visibility into the research submission pipeline.  
* **Knowledge and Technology Transfer Office (KTTO) Officers —** to confirm that IP evaluation and routing functions meet their operational requirements.  
* **Innovation & Technology Support Office (ITSO) —** to validate technical review stage requirements and document routing logic for Project-type submissions.  
* **Institutional Ethics Review Committee (IERC) and WIL Faculty —** to confirm that ethics review routing and data privacy features satisfy institutional and legal standards.  
* **Software Developers and System Architects —** to use this document as the primary reference for implementation and testing decisions.  
* **CIT-U Information Technology Administration —** to understand on-premise deployment constraints, infrastructure requirements, and security obligations.

  2. ## ***Scope***

**System Name:** Intelligent Research & IP System (IRIS)  
**Supersedes:** Intellectual Property Asset Management System v2.0 (IPAMS v2.0)

IPAMS v2.0 suffered from three critical limitations that made incremental remediation unfeasible: (1) severe performance degradation when concurrent user traffic exceeded ten individuals, rendering the system a bottleneck during peak submission periods; (2) an AI module that functioned as a stateless large language model wrapper with no institutional context, producing unreliable and unverifiable outputs; and (3) the absence of a structured, hierarchical approval workflow that mirrors CIT-U's actual governance structure, with no technical controls for compliance with the Data Privacy Act of 2012 (RA 10173). Following architectural review, a full reimplementation was determined to be the only viable path to address all three limitations simultaneously.

IRIS is a web-based research record management platform that organizes, manages, and tracks the lifecycle of intellectual property assets and research outputs produced by students, faculty, and research offices at CIT-U. The system encompasses the following core capabilities:

**Performance at Scale**. A Django REST Framework backend designed to sustain a minimum of 100 concurrent users at MVP deployment with response times not exceeding 2 seconds under load, enforced through request throttling and optimized database queries. The architecture is designed to scale to 1,000 concurrent users for enterprise-phase readiness.

**Type-Differentiated Submission Workflow**. IRIS accepts three classes of research submissions, each with its own document requirements and approval routing:

* **Proposal** — an early-stage research idea prior to execution. Reviewed exclusively by the student's assigned Faculty Adviser in an iterative approval loop until accepted or rejected.  
* **Thesis** / **Research** — a completed academic research paper or thesis. Routed through RDCO intake, then to IERC and KTTO in parallel, followed by RDCO final review.  
* **Project** — a completed project output (software system, prototype, or applied project), requiring an NDA in addition to standard documents. Routed through RDCO intake, then to ITSO (sequential), followed by IERC and KTTO in parallel, followed by RDCO final review.

At each decision point — RDCO intake, office review (IERC, KTTO, ITSO), and RDCO final review — authorized reviewers may approve, request revision, or reject outright. Outright rejection is distinct from a revision request and is reserved for submissions that are fundamentally out of scope, represent a serious compliance violation, or originate from ineligible submitters. Approved records are permanently archived in the RDCO institutional repository.

**Semantic Indexing Pipeline**. All submitted research PDFs are processed through a two-track indexing pipeline: a synchronous PostgreSQL full-text search index for keyword-based discovery, and an asynchronous vector embedding pipeline for semantic similarity search. Both the FTS index and vector embeddings are stored on-premise in PostgreSQL using the pgvector extension.

**RAG-Powered AI Services**. A Retrieval-Augmented Generation module provides: (a) a conversational chatbot for natural language queries against the institutional research library; and (b) a full-text paper summarizer with source-linked evidence for reviewer auditability. Vector search is executed on-premise via PostgreSQL pgvector. LLM inference is handled via a stateless cloud API (OpenAI GPT-4.1-mini) operating exclusively on anonymized, extracted text chunks. No raw files, personally identifiable information, or unprocessed IP disclosures are transmitted to external services, and no data is retained by the external provider.

**Role-Based Access Control and Security.** JWT-based session management with a 30-minute auto-expiry, role-differentiated access enforcing the institutional approval hierarchy, mandatory data privacy consent on all submissions, and an immutable audit log of all system events, in alignment with RA 10173\.

**KPI Dashboards.** Role-differentiated dashboards enabling students, staff reviewers, and administrators to monitor submission pipeline status, office review queues, and system-wide research output metrics, with exportable reports.

**Responsive Interface.** A fully redesigned frontend supporting both mobile and desktop screen sizes, replacing the fixed-layout interface of IPAMS v2.0.

IRIS shall NOT:

* Replace or integrate with CIT-U's existing Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) system, student information system, or grade management platform.  
* Manage academic records not classified as intellectual property or research outputs (e.g., enrollment data, financial transactions, grade records).  
* Transmit raw uploaded files, personally identifiable information, or unprocessed IP disclosures to any external cloud service. Cloud LLM APIs are used only for inference on anonymized, extracted text and operate under stateless conditions.  
* Provide legal advice, formal IP valuation, or binding commercialization assessments; the system supports workflow management and institutional recordkeeping only.

  3. ## ***Definitions, Acronyms and Abbreviations***

The following terms, acronyms, and abbreviations are used throughout this document. All system-level requirements shall be interpreted using the definitions below.

Table 1: Definitions, Acronyms and Abbreviations

| Term / Acronym | Definition |
| :---: | ----- |
| **IPAMS** | Intellectual Property Asset Management System \- the legacy web-based platform managed by CIT-U for submitting, reviewing, and archiving intellectual property records. |
| **IRIS** | Intelligent Research & IP System \- the reimplemented, AI-enhanced platform that supersedes IPAMS v2.0. |
| **RAG** | Retrieval-Augmented Generation \- an AI architecture that grounds large language model responses in a specific local knowledge base to reduce hallucination. |
| **LLM** | Large Language Model \- a deep-learning model trained on large text corpora to understand and generate natural language (e.g., GPT, LLaMA). |
| **NLP** | Natural Language Processing \- a branch of artificial intelligence concerned with enabling computers to understand and generate human language. |
| **FTS** | Full-Text Search \- a technique for querying unstructured text by indexing all words in a document corpus, enabling keyword-based search with relevance ranking. In IRIS, implemented using PostgreSQL's built-in tsvector indexing. |
| **Vector Embedding** | A numerical representation of text in high-dimensional space, generated by a machine learning model, that captures semantic meaning and enables similarity-based search. |
| **RDCO** | Research and Development Coordinating Office \- the CIT-U office responsible for final approval and archiving of all research and IP submissions. |
| **KTTO** | Knowledge and Technology Transfer Office \- the CIT-U office that evaluates the commercialization potential of intellectual property submissions. |
| **ITSO** | Innovation & Technology Support Office \- the CIT-U office handling technical review of research outputs. |
| **IERC** | Institutional Ethics Review Committee \- the CIT-U committee responsible for ethics compliance review of research submissions. |
| **Proposal** | A Record Type representing an early-stage research idea prior to execution. Reviewed by the Faculty Adviser only, in an iterative loop until approved or rejected. |
| **Thesis/Research** | A Record Type representing a completed academic research paper or thesis. Routed through RDCO intake → IERC \+ KTTO (parallel) → RDCO final review. |
| **Project** | A Record Type representing a completed project output (software system, prototype, or applied project). Requires an NDA. Routed through RDCO intake → ITSO → IERC → RDCO final review, with KTTO running in parallel throughout. |
| **NDA** | Non-Disclosure Agreement \- a required document for Project-type submissions, reviewed by ITSO. |
| **JWT** | JSON Web Token \- a compact, digitally signed token standard used for secure stateless session management in web applications. |
| **RBAC** | Role-Based Access Control \- a security mechanism that restricts system access and workflow permissions based on a user's assigned institutional role. |
| **RA 10173** | Republic Act 10173, the Data Privacy Act of 2012 \- the Philippine law governing the collection, storage, and processing of personal data. |
| **IP** | Intellectual Property \- creations of the mind such as research outputs, inventions, theses, and projects that may be protected under law. |
| **KPI** | Key Performance Indicator \- a measurable metric used to evaluate operational performance. In IRIS, KPI dashboards surface submission pipeline throughput, review stage durations, and research output volumes. |
| **MVP** | Minimum Viable Product \- the initial production-ready release of IRIS, implementing all core modules except KPI Dashboards, which are targeted for the subsequent delivery phase. |
| **API** | Application Programming Interface \- a defined set of protocols that allows software systems to communicate with each other. |
| **REST** | Representational State Transfer \- an architectural style for distributed web services using standard HTTP methods. |
| **PDF** | Portable Document Format \- the primary file format used for research document submissions in IRIS. |
| **SRS** | Software Requirements Specification \- this document; a comprehensive description of the system's intended behavior and constraints. |
| **SUS** | System Usability Scale \- a standardized 10-item questionnaire for measuring perceived usability of a system (scored 0–100). |
| **ERP** | Enterprise Resource Planning \- CIT-U's existing integrated administrative system, which IRIS does not interface with or replace. |

2. # **Overall Description**

   1. ## ***Product Perspective***

IRIS functions as a standalone but critical component of CIT-U's broader research and academic infrastructure. It is designed around a Hybrid-Cloud Architecture to balance regulatory compliance with high-scale computational demands.

The system flow begins at the Student Portal, where an author uploads a PDF disclosure. This document is immediately processed by the asynchronous Automatic Indexing module (powered by Celery), which extracts text using Docling and generates vector embeddings via an embedding API. The structured metadata, audit logs, and vector embeddings are all stored in an on-premise PostgreSQL database — the embeddings using the pgvector extension. This foundation powers the RAG Chatbot and Summarizer, allowing users to query the institutional knowledge base natively. From there, the document enters the Hierarchical Workflow Engine, traversing through sequential approval gates. Real-time pipeline analytics are aggregated and forwarded to the RDCO Dashboard for high-level monitoring.

To ensure data residency under RA 10173, all PDF files, relational data, and vector embeddings are stored strictly on-premise on local CIT-U servers. Only LLM embedding, reranking, and inference is offloaded to a stateless cloud API. The external LLM does not retain institutional IP for training and operates exclusively on anonymized, extracted text chunks.

External Software Dependencies: The system relies on several core external software components: the Django application framework, PostgreSQL with the pgvector extension for both relational data and vector search, Redis and Celery for asynchronous task queuing, Docling-serve for structured PDF text extraction, and the OpenAI API for LLM inference and embedding generation. (Detailed versioning is covered in Section 3.1.2.)

2. ## ***User Characteristics***

Table 2: User Characteristics

| User Class | Technical Level | Primary Interaction & System Role |
| :---: | :---: | ----- |
| **Students / Researchers** | Low–Medium | Uploading IP disclosures via the portal, signing data privacy consents, and engaging with the conversational chatbot for prior art and literature search.  |
| **Faculty Advisers** | Medium | Reviewing student submissions for academic merit, reading full-text AI summaries, and providing the initial digital sign-off to push the document up the pipeline.  |
| **IERC Members (Institutional Ethics Review Committee)** | Medium | Conducting ethical compliance reviews, ensuring research involving human subjects or sensitive data adheres to ethical standards and data privacy laws. |
| **ITSO Officers (Innovation & Technology Support Office)** | Medium–High | Conducting technical verification, patent drafting assessments, and deep prior-art checking to determine the protectability and novelty of the IP. |
| **KTTO Officers (Knowledge & Technology Transfer Office)** | Medium | Evaluating the commercial potential, industry partnership viability, and technology transfer readiness of the submitted intellectual property. |
| **RDCO Directors (Research & Development Coordinating Office)** | Low–Medium | Acting as the final institutional gateway. Monitoring the real-time KPI pipeline dashboard to identify bottlenecks across IERC, ITSO, and KTTO, and providing final archiving approval. |
| **System Administrators** | High | Managing local server health, overseeing vector DB maintenance, configuring RBAC permissions, and auditing security logs. |

3. ## ***Product Functions***

At a high level, IRIS provides the following major functional capabilities, each detailed in Section 3.2:

* **User Authentication & Session Management —** Secure login with JWT tokens and role-based dashboard routing  
* **IP Disclosure Submission —** Mobile-responsive web form for uploading and submitting research documents  
* **Document Management —** Versioned PDF upload requirements per record type, upload-level review status tracking, download request and approval flow, and soft deletion of records  
* **Load-Balanced Request Handling —** Traffic throttling and queuing under peak concurrent loads  
* **RAG-Powered Semantic Indexing —** Automatic PDF text extraction via Docling-serve, full-text keyword indexing, and vector embedding generation via the OpenAI embedding API  
* **Conversational RAG Chatbot —** Natural language querying of the institutional research library with inline citations  
* **Full-Text AI Document Summarization —** Structured summary generation with source-linked evidence for reviewer use  
* **Published Records Browse and Search —** Full-text keyword search and filter-based discovery of published records by year, record type, classification, PSCED code, and IP status  
* **Hierarchical Workflow Routing & Approval —** Type-differentiated multi-tier review pipeline with digital sign-offs, return-for-revision handling, and outright rejection at each decision point  
* **Notifications —** Real-time in-app pipeline event notifications routed to individual recipients or broadcast by role  
* **Security & Compliance —** JWT session management, DPA consent gateway, RBAC enforcement, and audit logging  
* **Bulk Record Import —** Staff-only Excel import for legacy record migration with a downloadable formatted template and row-level validation  
* **Storage Management —** Hierarchical institutional file storage with folder browsing, file upload, download, and role-gated access  
* **KPI Dashboard & Analytics —** Role-differentiated pipeline monitoring with exportable reports  
* **Admin Portal —** Centralized administration interface for user management, session revocation, audit log review, and AI index management

## ***2.4. 	Constraints***

The design and implementation of IRIS are bounded by the following technical, regulatory, and institutional constraints:

* **Regulatory Compliance:** The system must strictly adhere to the technical controls mandated by the Data Privacy Act of 2012 (RA 10173), necessitating encryption and explicit consent logging.  
* **Hardware and Hosting:** All raw PDF files, relational records, and audit logs must reside on existing on-premise CIT-U server hardware to guarantee data sovereignty. Vector embeddings are stored in a self-hosted vector database instance on-premise. No sensitive IP documents or personally identifiable information may be transmitted to or stored by any external cloud service.  
* **Framework:** The backend must utilize the Django framework on a newly established codebase. The legacy IPAMS v2.0 system was not extended or refactored, as it was determined to be architecturally unsuitable for the required scale and feature scope.  
* **Performance:** The system architecture must be designed to scale to a minimum of 1,000 concurrent users without session failure or severe degradation. The MVP deployment target is 100 concurrent users, with enterprise-phase validation at 1,000 concurrent users**.**  
* **University Authentication Integration:** Integration with existing CIT-U authentication infrastructure shall be implemented where available and technically feasible to prevent redundant credential management.  
* **Hybrid Data Residency (Cost vs. Security):** Due to the prohibitive hardware costs of running local LLM inference for CIT-U's large student population, the system is constrained to a hybrid model. Raw files and vector embeddings must be hosted on-premise. Third-party AI service providers may be used for RAG inference only. The system must ensure all external cloud interactions are stateless and that no external provider retains or trains on CIT-U's proprietary research data.

## ***2.5. 	Assumptions and Dependencies***

**Assumptions**

* **Provisional Workflow Design:** It is assumed that the specific routing order between IERC, ITSO, KTTO, and RDCO described in this document is provisional. The exact hierarchical logic will be refined and updated within the Django workflow engine following formal requirements-gathering interviews with the respective department heads.  
* **Hardware Capability:** It is assumed that existing CIT-U server hardware meets the standard computational specifications (CPU/RAM) necessary to host the Django application, PostgreSQL database, and Celery workers. Heavy AI computations are excluded from this assumption as they are offloaded to stateless cloud APIs.  
* **Legacy Data Access:** It is assumed that existing research records from the legacy IPAMS v2.0 system are available for migration into IRIS. No structural refactoring of the legacy codebase is assumed or required, as IRIS is built on a newly established codebase.  
* **Document requirement Definitions:** It is assumed that the required document requirements per record type (Proposal, Thesis/Research, Project) have been defined in coordination with RDCO and KTTO and are stable for the MVP release. Changes to document requirements after deployment will be handled through the administrative interface.  
* **Documentation:** Proper software documentation will be provided to all faculty, department officers, and staff prior to the system rollout. .  
* **Apache JMeter Availability:** It is assumed that Apache JMeter is installed and operational on the CIT-U development environment for use in pre-deployment stress testing.

**Dependencies**

* **Cloud API Availability and Graceful Degradation:** The RAG pipeline depends on the OpenAI API for LLM inference and embedding generation. In the event of a partial or total cloud service outage, the system shall degrade gracefully: all non-AI features remain fully operational; the RAG chatbot and summarizer interfaces shall display "AI features are temporarily unavailable. Please try again later."; PDF uploads shall be accepted and queued for deferred indexing; the system shall log all failed cloud API calls with timestamps and error codes in the audit trail.  
* **Docling-serve Availability:** PDF text extraction depends on a self-hosted Docling-serve instance running on-premise. If Docling-serve is unavailable, extraction tasks shall retry automatically. The system shall fall back to PyMuPDF and pytesseract for extraction until Docling-serve is restored.  
* **Celery and Redis Availability:** PDF text extraction, vector embedding generation, and email dispatch are processed as asynchronous Celery tasks brokered through Redis. If the Redis broker is unavailable, email delivery falls back to synchronous dispatch within the request cycle. Extraction and embedding tasks will queue and retry automatically when the broker is restored.  
* **Cloud API Cost Control:** Monthly cloud API expenditure shall not exceed a budget ceiling to be defined by CIT-U IT Administration prior to deployment.

3. # **Specific Requirements** 

   1. ## ***External Interface Requirements***

### ***3.1.1.	Hardware Interfaces***

IRIS does not interface with dedicated hardware peripherals such as printers, scanners, or biometric devices. However, the system imposes minimum hardware requirements on both the server-side deployment environment and client-side devices to guarantee stable operation under the concurrency and data residency constraints defined in Section 2.4. 

**Server-Side Hardware Requirements**

All sensitive IP records, relational data, uploaded PDF files, and vector embeddings must reside on CIT-U's on-premise server infrastructure in compliance with RA 10173\. For the Minimum Viable Product deployment, all services shall be co-located on a single physical server and isolated via Docker Compose containers. This consolidation reduces infrastructure cost and operational complexity while preserving the ability to scale horizontally by migrating individual containers to dedicated servers in future semesters as user load increases.

Table 3: IRIS Server Hardware Specifications

| Component | Specification | Rationale |
| ----- | :---: | ----- |
| CPU | 8-core processor (x86-64, 2.5 GHz or higher) | Supports Gunicorn workers, Celery task execution, PostgreSQL queries, and Redis operations concurrently under the 100-user MVP target. |
| RAM | 16 GB DDR4 | Allocated across services: \~4 GB Django/Gunicorn, \~4 GB PostgreSQL buffer pool, \~4 GB Celery workers, \~2 GB Redis, \~2 GB OS and headroom. |
| Storage | 500 GB NVMe SSD | Stores uploaded research PDF files on-premise, vector embedding index data, application logs, audit trail data, and Docker image layers. Sized to store up to 10,000 documents based on the maximum functional limit of 50MB per PDF. |
| Backup Storage | 500 GB secondary drive (internal HDD or USB) | Target for daily automated pg\_dump database backups, Qdrant snapshot exports, and weekly PDF file archive via rsync. Must be a separate physical drive from primary storage. |
| Network Interface | 1 Gbps Ethernet (internal) / 100 Mbps (external) | Internal bandwidth for inter-service communication; external bandwidth for cloud LLM API calls. |
| Operating System | Ubuntu Server 22.04 LTS |  Required for compatibility with Django, Python, Docker Compose, and the NGINX reverse proxy. |

**Docker Compose Service Isolation**

Each major system component runs as an isolated Docker container to enforce process separation and enable future horizontal scaling. The following containers are defined in the production docker-compose.yml:

Table 4: Docker Compose Service Map

| Container | Specification | Role | Scaling Path |
| ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- |
| *nginx* | nginx:1.24 | Reverse proxy, TLS termination, static file serving, rate limiting | Load balancer across multiple app servers |
| *web* | Custom Django image | Gunicorn WSGI application server (4 workers) | Add replicas behind NGINX |
| *celery-worker* | Custom Django image | Asynchronous task execution (PDF processing, embedding generation) | Add worker replicas |
| *celery-worker* | Custom Django image | General async tasks (email dispatch, notifications, audit logging) | Add worker replicas per queue |
| *celery-worker-rag* | Custom Django image | RAG pipeline tasks (PDF extraction via Docling-serve, embedding generation via OpenAI API) | Scale replicas independently from general workers |
| *celery-beat* | Custom Django image | Periodic task scheduler (cache warming, FTS index maintenance) | Single instance; not replicated |
| *docling* | doclingHQ/docling-serve:latest | Self-hosted on-premises REST API for PDF text extraction | Add replicas for extraction throughput |
| *db* | postgres:16 | Single PostgreSQL instance with pgvector extension for all relational data and vector embeddings	 | Migrate to dedicated server; add read replica |
| *redis* | redis:7 | Celery message broker and application cache. TTL varies by data type: 15 minutes for general query and embedding caches; 30 seconds for KPI dashboard analytics.	 | Migrate to dedicated instance |

**Backup Strategy**

Automated daily backups shall be configured via a cron job on the host server. The backup process runs pg\_dump against the PostgreSQL container and copies the output to the secondary backup drive. PDF file storage is backed up weekly via rsync. Backups are retained for a rolling 30-day window.

### ***3.1.2.	Software interfaces***

This section documents all software systems, frameworks, libraries, and external services that IRIS interfaces with or depends upon. Dependencies are categorized as either runtime dependencies, which are required for the system to operate in production, or development and validation dependencies, which are used exclusively during building, testing, and deployment and are not bundled with the deployed system.

**Backend Framework: Django**

The primary backend interface of IRIS is the Django web framework. Django provides the MVC architecture, ORM-based database abstraction layer, built-in session management, and the administrative interface used by System Administrators for user and role management. All REST API endpoints consumed by the React frontend and the RAG pipeline services are defined and served through Django's URL routing layer.

**Relational Database: PostgreSQL**

IRIS uses PostgreSQL as its relational database for all structured institutional data and as the vector store for document embeddings via the pgvector extension. The pgvector extension enables cosine similarity queries using HNSW indexes directly within PostgreSQL, eliminating the need for a separate vector database service. The PostgreSQL instance must reside strictly on-premise on CIT-U server hardware in compliance with RA 10173\.

**Docling-serve: PDF Text Extraction API**

Docling-serve is the on-premise PDF text extraction service used by IRIS. When a PDF is uploaded for a document requirement, the system queues a background Celery task that POSTs the raw PDF bytes to the self-hosted Docling-serve instance and receives structured Markdown text in return. Docling-serve handles text-layer PDFs, complex multi-column layouts, and scanned or image-based PDFs via its own internal OCR pipeline, eliminating the need for separate fallback extraction libraries. The extracted text is cleaned and stored in PdfExtraction.extracted\_text for use by the full-text search index (FR-M3-02) and the vector embedding pipeline (FR-M3-03). The HTTP response to the uploader is not blocked — extraction runs entirely in the background.

**Asynchronous Task Queue: Celery and Redis** 

Computationally intensive and time-consuming operations \-- including PDF text extraction, metadata extraction via LLM API, embedding generation, vector database indexing, and document summarization \-- are executed asynchronously through a Celery task queue backed by a Redis message broker. This prevents long-running background jobs from blocking Django's synchronous web workers and ensures that PDF uploads return an immediate confirmation to the user while processing continues in the background. Redis also serves as the application-level cache for frequent queries and embedding results.

**Web Server and Reverse Proxy: NGINX and WhiteNoise**

NGINX serves as the reverse proxy and load balancer sitting between the public internet (or university network) and the Gunicorn application server. It handles SSL/TLS termination, request routing to Gunicorn workers using a least-connections algorithm, CORS header management, and per-IP rate limiting at 100 requests per second. Upstream health checks are performed every 10 seconds; unhealthy Gunicorn workers are automatically removed from the routing pool. Django static files (admin interface assets, API browser resources) are served directly from the Gunicorn application process via WhiteNoise, which compresses and caches static files at startup without requiring a separate static file server or NGINX configuration for those assets.

**Security Middleware: django-axes** 

IRIS uses django-axes to enforce brute-force login protection at the application layer. django-axes monitors failed authentication attempts per IP address and per username, and automatically locks out accounts that exceed the configured failure threshold. Locked accounts are visible to System Administrators through the locked users management interface, and can be unlocked via the administrative unlock endpoint, which also clears the recorded access attempts. This mechanism operates independently of NGINX rate limiting and provides application-level defense against credential stuffing attacks.

The bulk record import feature allows System Administrators to migrate legacy research records by uploading a formatted Excel file. A downloadable import template is provided to staff to ensure submissions conform to the expected column structure.

### ***3.1.3.	Communications Interfaces***

This section documents all communication protocols, data formats, and network interfaces used by IRIS for internal and external system communication.

**1\. Client-Server API: RESTful HTTP/HTTPS**

All communication between the React frontend and the Django backend is conducted via RESTful HTTP/HTTPS using standard HTTP methods (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE). All API requests and responses use JSON as the data interchange format. HTTP traffic on port 80 is redirected immediately to HTTPS on port 443; no application data is transmitted over unencrypted HTTP. All API endpoints are versioned under the /api/v1/ path prefix to support forward compatibility with future system iterations.

**2\. Authentication: JWT Bearer Tokens**

User session state is transmitted exclusively through JSON Web Tokens (JWT) carried in the HTTP Authorization header using the Bearer token scheme. Tokens are signed using the HMAC-SHA256 algorithm using Django's simplejwt as specified in Section 1.2. No session cookies carrying authentication state are used. All protected API endpoints validate the JWT signature and expiry on every request. Tokens expire after 30 minutes of inactivity, after which the client is required to re-authenticate, consistent with the auto-logout requirement defined in Section 1.2.

**3\. Real-Time KPI Dashboard Updates: Polling**

The RDCO Director's KPI pipeline dashboard displays near-real-time data by polling the Django REST API at a configurable interval (default: 30 seconds). Dashboard analytics are aggregated server-side and cached in Redis with a 30-second TTL. WebSocket-based push updates may be implemented as a post-MVP enhancement if polling latency proves insufficient for stakeholder needs.

**4\. RAG Chatbot Delivery**

LLM-generated chatbot responses are returned to the client as a complete JSON response via the standard REST API. The chatbot interface displays a loading indicator while the LLM generates the response. As a post-MVP enhancement, Server-Sent Events (SSE) may be implemented to stream responses incrementally, reducing perceived latency to under 1 second for the first token.

**5\. Database Communication: Django ORM over PostgreSQL**

Internal communication between the Django application server and the PostgreSQL relational database is handled exclusively through Django's Object-Relational Mapper (ORM). The ORM communicates with PostgreSQL over the standard PostgreSQL wire protocol on port 5432, bound to localhost only. This port is not exposed to the university network or the public internet. No raw SQL queries are constructed from user input; all database interactions are parameterized through the ORM to prevent SQL injection.

**6\. Vector Database Communication: pgvector (PostgreSQL Extension)**

Vector storage and similarity search are handled by the pgvector extension running inside the same PostgreSQL instance as the rest of the application. There is no separate vector database service or additional network port. The Django ORM communicates with pgvector through the standard PostgreSQL connection (port 5432, bound to localhost only) using the pgvector-django integration, which provides a VectorField column type and the cosine distance operator (\<=\>).

Record embeddings are stored in the ai\_recordembedding table as vector(N) columns (dimensions set to match the configured embedding provider, e.g. 1536 for OpenAI text-embedding-3-small). An HNSW index on the embedding column enables approximate nearest-neighbour (ANN) similarity queries at scale. All vector upserts and similarity searches are issued as standard SQL via the Django ORM — no additional SDK or HTTP client is required beyond the existing database connection. All vector data consists exclusively of floating-point embedding vectors derived from record titles and abstracts; no raw PDF content or PII is stored in the embedding table.

**7\. External Cloud API Communication**

The RAG pipeline communicates with one confirmed external cloud service: the OpenAI API, used exclusively for LLM inference (GPT-4.1-mini) by the RAG chatbot (AskView) and the on-demand document summarizer (SummarizeView). Vector embedding generation will be handled by a third-party embedding API (provider TBD) and is documented separately once the provider is confirmed. Vector search is performed on-premise via the self-hosted pgvector extension within PostgreSQL.

All external API calls are stateless — no raw PDF content, PII, or institutional IP is retained by the external provider after the API response is returned. Only anonymized text (record titles, abstracts, and extracted document text) is transmitted. All calls are made over HTTPS and are subject to token bucket rate limiting at 50 requests per second with exponential backoff on HTTP 429 responses.

2. ## ***Functional Requirements***

Table 20: Functional Requirements

| FR-ID | Current Label | Functional Description |
| ----- | :---: | ----- |
| **FR-M1-01** | User Login and Session Management | The system shall authenticate users via email and password against the PostgreSQL user store. On success, a 30-minute JWT access token and a long-lived refresh token shall be issued via djangorestframework-simplejwt. The refresh token must be blacklisted on logout to prevent reuse. The system shall redirect unauthenticated requests to the login screen and redirect authenticated users away from the login screen. |
| **FR-M1-02** | API Request Throttling and Rate Limiting | The system shall enforce per-user and anonymous request rate limits on all REST endpoints using DRF's built-in throttling classes. Requests that exceed the configured threshold shall return HTTP 429\. Throttle windows and limits shall be configurable in Django settings without code changes. |
| **FR-M1-03** | Mobile-Responsive Interface Redesign | All pages of the React frontend shall render correctly on desktop (1280 px and above), tablet (768 px), and mobile (375 px) viewport widths using Tailwind CSS responsive utilities. No horizontal scrollbar shall appear at any supported viewport. Navigation elements shall collapse to a menu on narrow viewports. |
| **FR-M2-01** | IP Disclosure Submission Portal | The system shall provide a multi-step wizard form for student users to submit a new research record. The wizard shall collect: title, abstract, year accomplished, record type (fetched from the API), adviser (fetched from the API), authors (free-text chips), and co-owners (by user search). On final submission, the record shall be persisted with a status of draft and the submitting user recorded as the primary owner. |
| **FR-M2-02** | Document Download Request Flow | Authenticated users with appropriate role clearance shall be able to download individual uploaded document versions from their detail view. Staff roles shall be able to download any version; student owners may only download versions they uploaded. Downloads shall be served as binary file responses with the original filename preserved in the Content-Disposition header. |
| **FR-M2-03** | Document Soft-Deletion Flow | Record owners may request deletion of their own record; RDCO may approve or reject the request. Deletion shall be implemented as a soft delete (status set to pending\_delete, then to a tombstone state) rather than a hard database removal, ensuring audit history is preserved. Hard deletion shall require explicit staff confirmation. |
| **FR-M2-04** | Bulk Record Import via Excel | Staff users shall be able to upload an .xls or .xlsx workbook to batch-import legacy research records. The system shall use pyexcel-xls and pyexcel-xlsx to parse the workbook. Each row shall be validated against the same field rules as the single-record form. Rows that fail validation shall be reported back to the staff user in a structured error list; valid rows shall be committed as published records. |
| **FR-M2-05** | Published Records Browse and Full-Text Search | Any authenticated user shall be able to browse the paginated list of published research records and search by keyword. Search shall execute against the PostgreSQL SearchVectorField (weighted: title \= A, abstract \= B) backed by a GIN index. Results shall be ranked by relevance and returned with pagination metadata. The interface shall support filter controls for record type and year. |
| **FR-M2-06** | Institutional File Storage Management | Staff users shall be able to attach supplementary files (non-PDF attachments) to any record via the miscellaneous file upload endpoint. Attached files shall be listed on the record detail view. Staff may delete any attachment; owners may delete attachments they uploaded. All files shall be stored on the institutional on-premise file system under a structured directory path keyed by record ID. |
| **FR-M3-01** | PDF Upload and Text Extraction | When a user uploads a PDF file for a document requirement, the system shall enqueue a Celery task to extract plain text from the uploaded document. The task shall use OpenDataLoader as the primary extraction method. If primary extraction fails, the task shall fall back to PyMuPDF (fitz) as the secondary extractor. The extracted text shall be stored in the PdfExtraction model linked to the upload record. The task shall retry up to three times on transient failure before marking the extraction as failed |
| **FR-M3-02** | Full-Text Search (FTS) Indexing | The system shall maintain a SearchVectorField on each Record, updated via a post\_save signal whenever the record's title or abstract changes. The vector shall be built using Django's SearchVector with title weighted A and abstract weighted B. A GIN index on the field shall support sub-2-second keyword queries across the full record corpus. |
| **FR-M3-03** | Vector Embedding Storage | Upon successful text extraction, the system shall enqueue a Celery task (with a 60-second countdown to allow extraction to settle) that generates a fixed-dimension sentence embedding using a locally hosted sentence-transformers model. The embedding shall be serialized with pickle.dumps and stored in the RecordEmbedding.embedding BinaryField in PostgreSQL. An EmbeddingJob row shall track the status (queued, running, done, failed) for observability. The task shall retry up to three times on transient failure. |
| **FR-M4-01** | RAG Chatbot Query Processing and Conversation Management | The system shall expose a chat endpoint that accepts a user query, retrieves the top-N semantically similar records by computing cosine similarity between the query embedding and all stored RecordEmbedding vectors, and forwards the ranked context passages along with the query to the LLM API to generate a grounded response. Conversation history shall be maintained per session so the assistant can answer follow-up questions in context. |
| **FR-M4-02** | Full-Text AI Document Summarization | The system shall generate a structured four-part summary from a document's full text. Summaries shall not be persisted; they are generated on demand. |
| **FR-M5-01** | Document Routing and IP Evaluation Workflow | The system shall route submitted records through a pipeline of status stages determined by record type. Proposal records route through adviser review only. Thesis and Research records route: RDCO intake \-\> IERC review and KTTO review (parallel) \-\> RDCO final decision. RDCO intake → ITSO review → IERC review → RDCO final decision; KTTO runs in parallel throughout the ITSO and IERC stages. RDCO may reject a record at intake for ineligibility. Reviewing offices (IERC, KTTO, ITSO) may recommend rejection for serious violations. RDCO issues the final approve, revise, or reject decision. Status transitions shall be enforced server-side; client role shall be validated against the permitted transitions for each stage. |
| **FR-M5-02** | Auth PIN for Gated Record Access | Certain records may be marked as requiring PIN-based access authorization. The system shall generate a one-time PIN and deliver it to the requesting user. The PIN must be presented to access the gated content. The PIN shall be validated server-side; expired or already-used PINs shall be rejected. PIN generation and use events shall be logged in the audit trail. |
| **FR-M5-03** | Document-Level Review and Status Transitions | Each uploaded document version shall carry its own review status (e.g., For Application, Reviewed, Filed, Approved, Disapproved), managed by staff via the UploadReview endpoint. A reviewing office user may change the status of a document version within the stages they own. Status changes shall be timestamped and associated with the acting user. |
| **FR-M5-04** | Pipeline Event Notifications | The system shall dispatch in-app notifications to relevant parties at each workflow transition. Recipients and message content shall be determined by the transition type: submission received (Adviser notified for Proposals; RDCO notified for Thesis/Research/Project), review assigned (reviewing office notified), revision requested (owner notified), decision issued (owner and all reviewing offices notified). Notification delivery shall be logged so that failed deliveries can be identified. |
| **FR-M5-05** | Record IP Classification and Tagging | Staff users shall be able to tag a research record with one or more IP classification labels (e.g., Patent, Copyright, Trade Secret, Utility Model) after RDCO final review. Tagged classifications shall be visible on the record detail view and filterable in the browse interface. A record may carry multiple classifications. |
| **FR-M6-01** | JWT Token Enforcement and Session Lifecycle | All protected API endpoints shall require a valid JWT access token in the Authorization header. Tokens shall expire after 30 minutes. The system shall provide a token refresh endpoint that issues a new access token given a valid refresh token. On logout, the presented refresh token shall be blacklisted using simplejwt's token blacklist mechanism, preventing further use. |
| **FR-M6-02** | Role-Based Access Control Enforcement | The system shall enforce role-based permission checks on every API endpoint. The six roles \-- Student, Adviser, KTTO, RDCO, ITSO, IERC \-- shall map to distinct permission sets defined in core/permissions.py. No endpoint shall return data or permit actions above the requesting user's assigned role. Role checks shall be enforced server-side regardless of what the frontend renders. |
| **FR-M6-03** | Role Request and Approval Flow | Users may submit a request to be assigned a non-Student role. The request shall be held in a pending state and surfaced to staff administrators. An authorized staff member may approve or reject the request. On approval, the user's role shall be updated and the user notified. On rejection, the user shall receive a rejection notification with a reason. |
| **FR-M6-04** | Account Management (Lock, Unlock, Role Change) | Staff administrators shall be able to lock a user account (preventing login), unlock a locked account, and change a user's assigned role via the admin user management interface. Account state changes shall be recorded in the audit log. A locked user attempting to log in shall receive a clear error message indicating the account is inactive. |
| **FR-M6-05** | Active Session Monitoring and Revocation | Staff administrators shall be able to view a list of active user sessions (issued JWT refresh tokens). Administrators may revoke any active session, immediately blacklisting the associated refresh token so the affected user must re-authenticate. Revocation events shall appear in the audit log. |
| **FR-M6-06** | Data Privacy Consent and Audit Logging | The system shall record user consent to the data privacy notice (compliant with RA 10173\) at account registration. All security-relevant events \-- login, logout, failed login, PIN generation, PIN verification, document access, document upload, document download, document deletion, document rename, role change, account lock/unlock, session revocation \-- shall be written to the AuditEvent table with actor identity, event type, timestamp, and associated record ID (if applicable). The audit log shall be read-only to all roles except system administrators. |
| **FR-M7-01** | Role-Differentiated Pipeline Monitoring Dashboard | The system shall provide a dashboard view tailored to each staff role, displaying the records currently in their pipeline queue, average processing time per stage, and counts by status. Student users shall see a personal dashboard showing the status of their own submitted records. The dashboard shall refresh its data on page load and support manual refresh. |
| **FR-M7-02** | Report Generation and Export | Staff administrators shall be able to generate summary reports of research output by year, department, record type, and IP classification. Reports shall be exportable as .xlsx files using pyexcel-xlsx. Generated reports shall include aggregate counts, trend data, and a listing of records matching the selected filter criteria. |
| **FR-M8-01** | Admin Portal Overview and User Administration | Django Admin users shall have access to a centralized portal displaying quick-stat cards (total users, locked accounts, pending role requests, active sessions), a searchable and filterable user list, and per-user actions for locking/unlocking accounts and changing roles. All actions shall be recorded in the audit log. |
| **FR-M8-02** | Audit Log Management | Django Admin users shall be able to browse the full audit log, filter by event type, actor, and date range, and export the filtered results as an .xlsx file. The audit log shall be read-only; no editing or deletion of audit events is permitted by any role. |
| **FR-M8-03** | RAG and AI Index Administration | Django Admin users shall be able to monitor the embedding index status (total records, indexed count, last-run timestamp), trigger re-indexing of all records or a single record, and view the embedding job log filtered by status (queued, running, done, failed). Admin shall also be able to view and edit the RAG configuration (system prompt, LLM model, top-K, embedding model) via the RAGConfiguration singleton. (Note: RAGConfiguration model and config endpoint are deferred — currently returns 501.) |

### ***Module 1: Backend Optimization & Responsive UI***

This module covers user registration and authentication, secure session management via JWT tokens, role-based access gating, and brute-force protection, alongside a mobile-responsive interface that adapts to desktop, tablet, and mobile viewports, and API rate limiting to ensure platform stability under concurrent traffic.

#### **3.2.1.1 User Login and Session Management**

FR-ID: FR-M1-01

**Use Case Diagram**

*![][image1]*   
*Figure 1: User Login and Session Management Use Case Diagram*

**Use Case Description**

Use Case M1-1.1: Register Account

| Use Case | Register Account |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Actors** | Guest (Unregistered User) |
| **Description** | The system allows users to create an IRIS account using their institutional email, personal details, and data privacy consent. The system enforces the selection of a role (Student or Faculty) during registration, creates an unverified account with the chosen role, and dispatches an activation email. |
| **Preconditions** | The user has a valid institutional email address and has not previously registered with IRIS. |
| **Main Flow** | The user navigates to the registration page and fills in their institutional email, full name, password, and selects a role (Student or Faculty). The user selects their affiliated department or course and acknowledges the data privacy consent. The system validates all fields, ensures the email domain is an approved institution, and creates an unverified user account with the selected role. The system sends a time-limited email verification link to the provided address. The system displays a confirmation prompting the user to check their email. |
| **Alternative Flow** | **Validation Failure:** At Step 3, if the email is not an institutional email, is already registered, the password is too weak, consent is not acknowledged, or a required field is missing, the system returns inline field errors and the account is not created. |
| **Postconditions** | An unverified user account exists in the system with the selected role. A verification email has been dispatched. |

Use Case M1-1.2: Verify Email Address

| Use Case | Verify Email Address |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Actors** | Registered (Unverified) User |
| **Description** | The system verifies the ownership of an institutional email address through a time-limited activation link sent to the user. Verification is required before the user can log in and access the platform. |
| **Preconditions** | The user has completed registration and received a verification email. |
| **Main Flow** | The user opens the verification email and clicks the activation link.  The system validates the link's authenticity and checks that it has not expired (3-day window).  The system marks the account as email-verified.  The system displays an "Email verified — awaiting administrator role approval" confirmation. |
| **Alternative Flow** | **Expired or Invalid Link:** At Step 2, if the link has expired or has been tampered with, the system displays an error and the account remains unverified. |
| **Postconditions** | The user account is marked as verified. The user may log in once an administrator approves their role request. |

Use Case M1-1.3: User Login and Session Management

| Use Case | User Login and Session Management |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Actors** | Any System User |
| **Description** | The system establishes an authenticated session for users accessing the IRIS platform. The system validates credentials, issues a secure JSON Web Token (JWT), and routes the user to their role-specific dashboard based on their registered role. |
| **Preconditions** | The IRIS system is online, and the user has a registered and email-verified institutional account. |
| **Main Flow** | The user navigates to the IRIS login page via a web browser (mobile or desktop). The user enters their institutional email and password. The system validates the credentials and issues a JWT access token (30-minute validity) and a refresh token (7-day validity). The system records a login event in the audit log. The system redirects the user to their role-specific dashboard. |
| **Alternative Flow** | **Invalid Credentials and Account Lockout:** At Step 3, if the credentials do not match, the system increments the failed login counter and displays a generic "Invalid email or password" error. After 3 consecutive failures from the same account and IP address, the system locks the account for 10 minutes, displays an "Account Locked" notification, and logs a security event in the audit trail. The lockout lifts automatically after 10 minutes.  **Unverified Account:** At Step 3, if the account has not completed email verification, the system returns an "Email not verified" error and does not issue tokens.  **Admin-Locked Account:** At Step 3, if an administrator has manually locked the account, the system returns an "Account is locked" error. |
| **Postconditions** | A secure, authenticated session is started for the user. JWT tokens are stored in the browser. |

Use Case M1-1.4: Silent Token Refresh

| Use Case | Silent Token Refresh |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Actors** | Authenticated User |
| **Description** | When the user's short-lived access token expires, the system transparently issues a new token pair using the stored refresh token, without interrupting the session or requiring a new login. |
| **Preconditions** | The user is logged in with a valid, non-expired refresh token stored in the browser. |
| **Main Flow** | An API request receives an HTTP 401 response indicating the access token has expired. The system reads the stored refresh token from the browser. The system requests a new token pair from the server. The server validates the refresh token, issues a new access and refresh token, and permanently invalidates the old refresh token.  The system saves both new tokens and transparently retries the original failed request. |
| **Alternative Flow** | **Missing or Invalid Refresh Token:** At Steps 2–3, if no refresh token is found or the token is expired, invalid, or already invalidated, the system clears all session data from the browser and redirects the user to the login page. |
| **Postconditions** | A new token pair is active. The old refresh token is permanently invalidated. The original request completes without user intervention. |

Use Case M1-1.5: Log Out

| Use Case | Log Out |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Actors** | Authenticated User |
| **Description** | The user ends their IRIS session. The system invalidates the refresh token server-side to prevent reuse and clears all local session data from the browser. |
| **Preconditions** | The user is authenticated with an active session. |
| **Main Flow** | The user clicks the "Sign Out" button. The system sends the current refresh token to the server for invalidation.  The server blacklists the refresh token and records a logout event in the audit log. The system removes all tokens from the browser and redirects the user to the login page. |
| **Alternative Flow** | **Already-Invalidated Token:** If the refresh token has already expired or been blacklisted, the server discards the error and still returns success. The local session is cleared regardless. |
| **Postconditions** | The refresh token is permanently blacklisted. All local session data is cleared. A logout event is recorded in the audit log. |

Use Case  M1-1.6: Admin Session Revocation

| Use Case | Admin Session Revocation |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Actors** | Admin |
| **Description** | An administrator force-terminates any active user session by revoking the associated JWT. The affected user is logged out on their next request. |
| **Preconditions** | The administrator is authenticated with staff privileges. At least one active session exists in the system. |
| **Main Flow** | The administrator navigates to the Active Sessions management screen. The administrator selects a session and confirms the revocation. The system force-blacklists the JWT by its unique token identifier.  The system records the administrative action in the audit log.  The targeted user is redirected to the login page upon their next request. |
| **Alternative Flow** | **Session Not Found:** If the selected session token no longer exists or has already expired, the system returns a not-found error and no further action is taken. |
| **Postconditions** | The targeted user's JWT is permanently blacklisted. The user is effectively logged out upon their next API interaction. |

Use Case M1-1.7: Change Password

| Use Case | Change Password |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Actors** | Authenticated User |
| **Description** | An authenticated user updates their account password from within the application. The system verifies the current password before accepting the new one. |
| **Preconditions** | The user is logged in with an active session. |
| **Main Flow** | The user navigates to their account settings and selects "Change Password."  The user enters their current password and a new password with confirmation.  The system verifies that the current password is correct and that the new password meets the minimum strength requirement. The system updates the password and displays a confirmation. |
| **Alternative Flow** | **Incorrect Current Password:** At Step 3, if the current password does not match the stored credential, the system returns a validation error and the password is not changed.  **Password Too Weak:** At Step 3, if the new password does not meet the minimum length requirement, the system returns a field-level error. |
| **Postconditions** | The user's password has been updated. Existing sessions remain active. |

#### **3.2.1.2 API Request Throttling and Rate Limiting**

FR-ID: FR-M1-02

**Use Case Diagram**

*![][image11]* 

*Figure 11: API Request Throttling and Rate Limiting Use Case Diagram* 

**Use Case Description**

Table M1-2.1: API Request Throttling and Rate Limiting

| Use Case | API Request Throttling and Rate Limiting |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Actors** | Authenticated User, Anonymous Client, Admin |
| **Description** | The system enforces rate limits on all API requests to prevent abuse and ensure service availability. Anonymous requests are limited by IP address, authenticated requests by user identity, and repeated login failures trigger a temporary account lockout. |
| **Preconditions** | The IRIS API is running and available to clients. |
| **Main Flow** | A client sends a request to any IRIS API endpoint. The system evaluates the client's request count against the applicable limit of 60 requests per minute or 6,000 requests per 10 minutes for users. If the limit has not been reached, the request counter is incremented and the request proceeds normally. The system returns the requested resource. |
| **Alternative Flow** | **Rate Limit Exceeded:** At Step 2, if the client has reached their daily limit, the system rejects the request with an HTTP 429 Too Many Requests response and includes a Retry-After header indicating when the client may resume.  **Brute-Force Lockout:** If a user fails to authenticate 3 consecutive times from the same email and IP combination, the system locks the account for 10 minutes and returns an HTTP 403 Forbidden response. An administrator may manually unlock the account before the window expires. |
| **Postconditions** | Valid requests within the limit are served. Clients that exceed the limit are informed of the retry window. Accounts subjected to brute-force attempts are temporarily locked. |

Use Case M1-3.1: Mobile-Responsive Interface

| Use Case | Mobile-Responsive Interface |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Actors** | Desktop User (≥1280px), Tablet User (768–1279px), Mobile User (\<768px) |
| **Description** | The IRIS interface adapts its navigation layout to the user's viewport size without horizontal scrolling or content overflow. Desktop users see a full labeled sidebar, tablet users see a compact icon-only rail, and mobile users access navigation through a collapsible drawer. |

On tablet (768–1279px): a compact icon-only navigation rail is permanently visible; labels, section headings, and notification badges are hidden. c. On mobile (\<768px): the sidebar is hidden off-screen, the content occupies the full width, and a hamburger button is visible in the header. |
| **Alternative Flow** | **Mobile Drawer Interaction:** On mobile, tapping the hamburger button slides the sidebar drawer into view with a backdrop overlay. The drawer closes when the user taps a navigation link, taps the backdrop, or taps the close button. |
| **Postconditions** | The user can navigate to all application destinations at any supported viewport width. No horizontal scrollbar appears at any supported screen size. |

### ***Module 2: Document Lifecycle & CRUD Operations***

This module covers the full lifecycle of a research record, from creating a draft through a multi-step submission wizard, uploading and versioning documents, submitting for review, and managing download and deletion requests, as well as bulk staff imports, keyword search across published records, and soft deletion with a preserved audit trail.

#### **3.2.2.1 Record Types, Department Templates, and Office Checklists**

FR-ID: FR-M2-01

**Use Case Diagram**  
**![][image17]**    

*Figure : Record Types, Department Templates, and Office Checklists Use Case Diagram*

**Use Case Description**

Use Case M2-1.1: Manage Record Types

| Use Case | Manage Record Types |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Actors** | Admin |
| **Description** | Staff administrators define the types of research records recognized by the system (e.g., Thesis, Proposal, Project). This foundational setup dictates what fields and workflows apply to submissions. |
| **Preconditions** | The user is authenticated with an Admin role. |
| **Main Flow** | Admin navigates to Settings \> Record Types. Admin creates, updates, or deletes a Record Type. System saves the changes. |
| **Alternative Flow** | **Validation Error:** If required fields are missing or duplicate, the system shows an error message, and changes are not saved. **Delete Record Type in Use:** If the Admin attempts to delete a Record Type that is currently assigned to existing records, the system prevents the deletion and shows an error message. |
| **Postconditions** | The new or updated Record Type is available for users to select during record submission. If deleted, it is no longer available for new submissions. |

Use Case M2-1.2: Manage Department Templates

| Use Case | Manage Department Templates |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Actors** | Admin, Adviser |
| **Description** | Administrators define the specific documents required for a given Record Type within a specific Department. When a Department has no custom template for a record type, the system falls back to a default template (where department \= NULL), preserving backward compatibility. |
| **Preconditions** | The user is authenticated with an Admin role; the target Record Type and Department exist. |
| **Main Flow** | Admin selects a Record Type and a Department (or "Global Default"). Admin adds a new Department Template entry (e.g., "Software Requirements Specification"). Admin marks the template as is\_required=True (mandatory) or False (optional). Admin sets the sort\_order for display ordering. System saves the template and enforces it on future submissions from that department. |
| **Alternative Flow** | **Duplicate Template:** If the Admin attempts to add a template with a name that already exists for the same Record Type \+ Department combination, the system returns an error message. **No Department Templates:** If a department has no templates for a record type, the system falls back to the global default templates. |
| **Postconditions** | The department template is saved and will be enforced for the selected Record Type \+ Department during record submissions. |
| **Backward Compatibility Rules**  | **Drafts and Declined Records:** Must comply with any newly added mandatory templates before they can be submitted or resubmitted. **Published Records:** Are grandfathered in and do not have their status revoked if a new template is added post-submission. |

Use Case M2-1.3: Manage Office Checklists

| Use Case | Manage Department Templates |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Actors** | Office Admin (KTTO, IERC, RDCO, ITSO) |
| **Description** | Office administrators define the documents their office requires from researchers during the review pipeline. These are stage-gated requirements, they are NOT needed at initial submission but become relevant only when the record reaches the office's review stage. Each checklist item can optionally be scoped to a specific Record Type, or left unscoped (applies to all types). |
| **Preconditions** | The user is authenticated with an Office Admin role. |
| **Main Flow** | Office Admin navigates to Settings \> Office Checklists. Office Admin selects their office (e.g., KTTO). Office Admin adds a new checklist item (e.g., "Non-Disclosure Agreement"). Office Admin optionally selects a Record Type scope (or leaves it as "All Types"). Office Admin marks the item as is\_required=True (mandatory for clearance) or False (optional). The system saves the checklist item. |
| **Alternative Flow** | **Duplicate Checklist Item:** If an item with the same name already exists for the same office \+ record type combination, the system returns an error. |
| **Postconditions** | The department template is saved and will be enforced for the selected Record Type \+ Department during record submissions. |
| **Backward Compatibility Rules**  | **Drafts and Declined Records:** Must comply with any newly added mandatory templates before they can be submitted or resubmitted. **Published Records:** Are grandfathered in and do not have their status revoked if a new template is added post-submission. |

Use Case M2-1.4: Manage Office Checklist Rules

| Use Case | Manage Office Checklist Rules |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Actors** | Office Admin (KTTO, IERC, RDCO, ITSO) |
| **Description** | Office administrators set up smart, conditional rules for their checklist items. Instead of asking every researcher for the exact same documents, admins can create "If-Then" logic (e.g., \*If\* the research is for commercialization, \*Then\* require a Market Analysis). If a checklist item has no rules, it applies to everyone. If it has multiple rules, all of them must be true for the document to be required. |
| **Preconditions** | The user is authenticated with an Office Admin role; the target checklist item exists. |
| **Main Flow** | Office Admin opens a checklist item's detail page. Office Admin clicks "Add Rule." Office Admin selects a field (e.g., for\_commercialization), an operator (e.g., is\_true), and a value. System saves the rule and attaches it to the checklist item. Office Admin can add multiple rules (AND logic) or remove existing rules. |
| **Alternative Flow** | **Invalid Field/Operator**: If the selected field or operator is not in the allowed list, the system returns a validation error. |
| **Postconditions** | The rule is saved. Future materializations of this checklist item will evaluate the rule before creating a RecordChecklistItem. |

#### **3.2.2.2 Record Submission**

FR-ID: FR-M2-02

**Use Case Diagram**

**Use Case Description**

Use Case M2-2.1: Create IP Disclosure Draft

| Use Case | Create IP Disclosure Draft |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Actors** | Record Owner (Student or Adviser) |
| **Description** | The record owner initiates a new IP disclosure by completing a multi-step submission wizard. The wizard collects record metadata, authors, co-owners, and document uploads. On completion, the system saves the record as a draft and assigns the submitting user as the primary owner. |
| **Preconditions** | The user is authenticated with a Student or Adviser role. |
| **Main Flow** | The owner navigates to "Add Record" and opens the submission wizard. The owner enters Title, Abstract, Year Accomplished, and Year Completed. The owner selects a Record Type; if the type is Proposal, an Adviser must also be selected. The owner adds author names as free-text chips and searches for co-owners by name or email. The owner uploads required documents for the selected record type. The owner completes the wizard; the system creates the record with pipeline\_status \= "draft" and records the owner as the primary RecordOwner. |
| **Alternative Flow** | **Validation Error**: At any step, missing required fields or invalid values produce inline errors; the owner cannot advance until they are resolved. **Proposal without Adviser**: At Step 3, if Record Type is Proposal and no Adviser is selected, the system prevents advancing and shows "Adviser is required for Proposals." |
| **Postconditions** | A draft record exists in the system. The submitting user is the primary owner. The record appears on the owner's My Records page with status Draft. |

Use Case M2-2.2: Submit Record for Review

| Use Case | Submit Record for Review |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Actors** | Record Owner (Student or Adviser) |
| **Description** | The record owner explicitly submits a saved draft (or a revised declined record) into the institutional review pipeline. The system routes the record to the appropriate first-stage reviewer based on the record type and notifies them. |
| **Preconditions** | The owner is authenticated; the record has pipeline\_status \= "draft" or "declined" (revision requested); the record has a Record Type assigned; Proposal records have an Adviser assigned. |
| **Main Flow** | The owner opens a draft (or declined) record from the My Records page and clicks "Submit for Review." The system validates that a Record Type is set and, for Proposals, that an Adviser is assigned. The system advances the pipeline status: Proposal → adviser\_review — the assigned Adviser is notified by email and in-app; Thesis/Research or Project → rdco\_intake — the RDCO role is notified by email and in-app. The owner is shown a confirmation: "Record submitted. The \[Adviser / RDCO\] has been notified." |
| **Alternative Flow** | **Already in Pipeline:** If pipeline\_status is not draft or declined, the system returns an error: "Record is in '…' status and cannot be submitted."  **No Record Type:** The system returns "A record type must be selected before the record can be submitted."  **Proposal without Adviser:** The system returns "An adviser must be assigned before a Proposal can be submitted."  **Resubmission after Decline:** If pipeline\_status \= "declined", the owner may click "Resubmit" — the system clears all previous clearance records and re-enters the pipeline at the first stage for the record type. |
| **Postconditions** | The record pipeline status is updated to the first review stage. The assigned reviewer receives a notification. |

#### **3.2.2.3 Document Version Management**

FR-ID: FR-M2-03  
![][image26]   
*Figure \#\#: Document Download Request Flow Use Case Diagram*

**Use Case Description**

Use Case M2-3.1: Upload Revised Document

| Use Case | Upload Revised Document |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Actors** | Record Owner |
| **Description** | When a record is declined and returned for revisions, the owner uploads corrected files. The system automatically stacks the new file as an incremented version (e.g., v2) under the exact same Upload Requirement, preserving chronological history without spawning redundant buckets. |
| **Preconditions** | The user is authenticated as the Record Owner, and the record is in a "Declined" or "Draft" state. |
| **Main Flow** | The owner navigates to the Documents tab of a declined record. The owner drops a new file into the existing Upload Requirement bucket. The system saves the file and increments the version number. |
| **Alternative Flow** | **Invalid File:** If the uploaded file exceeds the size limit or is an unsupported format, the system rejects it and shows an error message. |
| **Postconditions** | A new version of the document is saved and stacked chronologically under the existing requirement. |

Use Case M2-3.2: View Version History

| Use Case | View Version History |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Actors** | Record Owner, Reviewers (Staff) |
| **Description** | Users view all past versions of a specific document stacked chronologically under its Requirement. |
| **Preconditions** | The user is authenticated and has permission to view the record (Owner or Reviewer). |
| **Main Flow** | User opens the Documents tab. The system retrieves all Upload Requirements and their associated uploaded file versions. The system lists all Upload Requirements. Under each requirement, it displays the chronological history of uploaded versions (v1, v2). |
| **Alternative Flow** | **No Versions Uploaded:** If an optional requirement has no uploaded files, the system displays an empty state for that requirement. |
| **Postconditions** | The user successfully views the complete version history of the documents. |

Use Case M2-3.3: Delete Document Version

| Use Case | Delete Document Version |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Actors** | Record Owner, Staff |
| **Description** | Users view all past versions of a specific document stacked chronologically under its Requirement. |
| **Preconditions** | The user is authenticated and has permission to view the record (Owner or Reviewer). |
| **Main Flow** | The user clicks "Delete" on a document version. System checks permission: owners can delete outdated versions while the record is in Draft phase. The latest version requires admin (Staff) permission to delete. The system physically removes the file from storage and the database row. |
| **Alternative Flow** | **Insufficient Permissions:** If an Owner attempts to delete the latest version, or a version while the record is locked in review/published, the system denies the request and shows an error. |
| **Postconditions** | The specified document version is permanently deleted and removed from the version history. |
