Use Case M2-4.1: Document Download and Access Management

| Use Case | Download or View Own Document |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Actors** | Record Owner, Staff |
| **Description** | A record owner (any co-owner) or staff member may view a document version in-browser or download it directly, without going through an approval process. The DocumentsPage provides both actions via authenticated blob API calls. |
| **Preconditions** | The user is authenticated; the target document upload exists in the system; the user is a record co-owner or staff. |
| **Main Flow** | The user opens the DocumentsPage for a record. The system checks permission: any record co-owner or staff role.  a. **View:** The user clicks "View", the system serves the file with viewable format and the browser renders the PDF inside a fullscreen PdfViewer modal  b. **Download:** The user clicks "Download", the system serves the file with downloadable format and the browser saves the file. All requests are authenticated blob calls (binary file download) so the session is validated on every file access. |
| **Alternative Flow** | **Insufficient Permission:** At Step 2, if the user is not a record co-owner and is not a staff member, the system returns Permission Denied error |
| **Postconditions** | The file is viewed in-browser or downloaded to the user's device. A DOWNLOAD audit event is recorded. |

Use Case M2-4.2: Document Download Request

| Use Case | Document Download Request |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Actors** | Authenticated User (requester), Staff (KTTO / RDCO) |
| **Description** | An authenticated user who does not own a record requests access to download its files. Staff review the request and either approve (granting the user access, notified by email) or decline (notified in-app). |
| **Preconditions** | The requester is authenticated; the target record exists with \`published\` |
| **Main Flow** | The requester opens a published record and clicks "Request Download Access." The system creates a DownloadRequest marked as pending and broadcasts an in-app notification to KTTO and RDCO staff. A staff member reviews the request and clicks "Approve." The system sets marked as approved, records the reviewer, and sends an email notification to the requester. The requester can now download the record's documents directly. |
| **Alternative Flow** | **Staff Declines:** At Step 3, the staff member clicks "Decline." The system sets marked as declined, records the reviewer, and sends an in-app notification to the requester. The requester cannot download the documents. **Duplicate Request:** If the requester already has a pending or approved request for the same record, the system returns Validation error. |
| **Postconditions** | The DownloadRequest is updated to approved or declined. The requester is notified of the decision. |

Table M2-5: Delete Uploaded Document Version

| Use Case | Delete Uploaded Document Version |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Actors** | Record Owner, Staff |
| **Description** | A record owner deletes an uploaded document version they submitted. When the record is in the draft phase, the owner can only delete outdated versions; the latest version requires admin permission to delete. The physical file is removed from storage and the database row is deleted. |
| **Preconditions** | The user is authenticated; the document record exists. |
| **Main Flow** | The user clicks "Delete" on a document version in the record's document section. The system checks permission: the user must be the record owner or a staff member. The system checks the version constraint: if the user is the owner and the record is in draft phase, they cannot delete the latest version. The system deletes the physical file from storage and removes the document record database row. A DELETE audit event is logged. |
| **Alternative Flow** | **Insufficient Permission:** At Step 2, if the user is neither the record owner nor a staff member, the system returns Permission Denied error. **Owner Attempts to Delete Latest Version:** At Step 3, if the requester is an owner and they attempt to delete the latest version, the system returns Validation error "Cannot delete the latest version without admin permission." |
| **Postconditions** | The document version and its physical file are permanently removed. The DELETE event is recorded in the audit log. |

FR-ID: FR-M2-05

**Use Case Description**

Use Case M2-5.1: Record Soft-Deletion

| Use Case | Document Soft-Deletion Flow |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Actors** | Record Owner (primary), RDCO Staff |
| **Description** | A record owner requests soft-deletion of a published (public) record. Published records added to the IRIS directory require RDCO approval via a deletion request before they can be removed. For drafts and non-published records, Use Case M2-5 rules apply. Soft deletion marks the record as deleted in the database without physically removing it, preserving the audit trail. |
| **Preconditions** | The record exists and is published; the owner is authenticated and is the primary owner or a staff member. |
| **Main Flow** | The owner opens their published record and clicks "Request Deletion," providing a reason. The system creates a deletion request with status marked as pending and sets the record's status to marked for deletion. RDCO reviews the deletion request in the staff queue. **Approve:** RDCO clicks Approve → the system sets the record as marked as deleted, records the deletion time and the user who deleted it (soft delete), and notifies the owner. **Decline:** RDCO clicks Decline → the system sets the deletion request status to declined, restores the record to published, and notifies the owner. |
| **Alternative Flow** | **Cancel Deletion:** The owner can cancel their deletion request before RDCO reviews it, restoring the record to published status. |
| **Postconditions** | The record is either soft-deleted (marked as deleted, excluded from all queries) or restored to published. The owner is notified. The audit trail is preserved. |

Use Case M2-6.1: Bulk Record Import via Excel

| Use Case | Bulk Record Import via Excel |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Actors** | Staff (primary), System |
| **Description** | Staff bulk-import legacy research records from a formatted Excel workbook. The system parses each row using pyexcel, validates required fields, and commits valid rows directly as published records (bypassing the review pipeline, as staff are the implicit reviewers for legacy data). Rows with errors are skipped and reported. |
| **Preconditions** | The user is authenticated as Staff; the file is a valid .xls or .xlsx workbook formatted according to the IRIS import template. |
| **Main Flow** | Staff downloads the formatted import template via GET /records/download\_template/. Staff fills in legacy record rows following the column rules. Staff uploads the workbook via POST /records/import\_excel/. The system detects the file type (.xls or .xlsx) and parses it using pyexcel-xls / pyexcel-xlsx. Each row is validated: Title is required; Record Type defaults to "Project" if blank; Boolean columns accept TRUE / FALSE / YES / NO / 1 / Processing stops when the first cell of a row contains "END OF RECORDS." Valid rows are committed as published records (published). The system returns a structured import log: rows created, rows skipped, and per-row error messages. |
| **Alternative Flow** | **Invalid File:** The workbook cannot be opened → "Could not open file" error returned immediately; no rows are processed. **Missing Title:** Row has no Title value → row skipped; "Row N: Title is required" added to error log. **All Rows Invalid:** 0 records created; full error log returned. |
| **Postconditions** | Valid rows exist as published records visible in the Published Records list. Staff receive a creation count and error log for audit. |

### ***Module 3: Semantic Indexing***

This module covers the automated processing pipeline that makes research records discoverable, including PDF text extraction via Docling, full-text search indexing using PostgreSQL weighted search vectors, and vector embedding generation for semantic similarity queries.

#### **3.2.3.1 PDF Upload and Text Extraction**

**FR-ID: FR-M3-01**

| **Preconditions** | A PDF document has been successfully uploaded to the system. |
| **Main Flow** | The user uploads a PDF document.  The system sends the document to an external extraction service. The system receives the extracted text.  The system cleans and formats the text.  The cleaned text is stored in the database. |
| **Alternative Flow** | **Extraction Failure:** If the extraction service fails, the system automatically retries a few times. **Permanent Failure:** If all retries fail, the document is marked as failed, and the user is notified. |
| **Postconditions** | The extracted text is available for FTS indexing (FR-M3-02) and semantic search (FR-M3-03). |

#### **3.2.3.2 Full-Text Search (FTS) Indexing**

**FR-ID: FR-M3-02**

**Use Case Diagram**

![][image54]   

*Figure 42:Full-Text Search (FTS) Indexing Use Case Diagram*

**Use Case Description**

Use Case M3-2.1: Automatic Search Index Update

| Use Case | Automatic FTS Index Update |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Actors** | System |
| **Description** | To ensure that users can always find the most up-to-date information, the system continuously monitors the library of records. Whenever a new record is uploaded, an existing record's details are modified, or the text extraction process for a document finishes, the system automatically rebuilds the search index for that specific item. To provide the best search results, the system organizes this information, giving the highest importance to the record's title, secondary importance to the abstract, and standard importance to the full document text. |
| **Preconditions** | A user has successfully created a new record, updated an existing record's information, or the system has just finished extracting text from an uploaded document. |
| **Main Flow** | A trigger event occurs (e.g., a record is saved or text extraction completes). The system gathers all the searchable information for that record, including the title, abstract, and any extracted document text. The system applies a relevance weighting to the information, ensuring that title matches will rank higher than deep text matches in future searches. The system updates its central search directory with this newly organized information. The updated information becomes immediately available for users performing keyword searches. |
| **Alternative Flow** | **Indexing Error:** If an unexpected error occurs while trying to update the search directory, the system logs the error for administrators. The original record remains safe, and the system will automatically attempt to update the search directory again the next time that record is modified. |
| **Postconditions** | The record's latest information is accurately reflected in the search directory, allowing users to discover it through keyword searches based on its title, abstract, or full document text. |

Use Case M3-2.2: Keyword Search on Records

| Use Case | Keyword Search on Published Records |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Actors** | User |
| **Description** | Users can explore the library of published records by entering specific keywords or phrases. The system scans through the organized search directory checking titles, abstracts, and full document texts to find the best matches. It then presents these matches to the user, ordering them so that the most relevant and accurate results appear first. |
| **Preconditions** | The user is authenticated and there is at least one published record available in the system's search directory. |
| **Main Flow** | The user navigates to the search page and enters one or more keywords into the search bar. The system analyzes the user's input to understand the search intent. The system scans the central search directory for any records that contain the requested keywords. The system calculates a relevance score for each matching record (e.g., scoring a title match higher than a match deep inside a document). The system returns the matching records to the user, sorted from highest to lowest relevance. |
| **Alternative Flow** | **No Results:** If the system cannot find any records containing the keywords, it returns an empty list and displays a helpful "No records found" message to the user.  **Invalid Search Input:** If the user enters an unsupported search query, the system safely ignores the invalid parts or returns an empty result set without crashing. |
| **Postconditions** | Matching published records are displayed, ranked by relevance. |

| Use Case | Trigger Embedding for a Single Record |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Actors** | Staff / Admin, System |
| **Description** | To power advanced semantic search, the system automatically generates AI vector embeddings for records as soon as they are published and their text extraction is complete. Staff can also manually trigger this processing if needed. |
| **Preconditions** | A record is marked as published, its text extraction is finished, and the internal AI gateway is connected to the external AI service. |
| **Main Flow** | The system detects that a record has been published and its text extraction is complete, or a staff member manually triggers the process. The system adds an embedding request to an asynchronous background job queue. The background task retrieves the record's text and applies the currently configured formatting or chunking strategy. The system securely sends the prepared text through the internal AI gateway to an external AI service. The external AI service processes the text and returns the vector embeddings. The system stores the generated embeddings in the database, linking them to the record. |
| **Alternative Flow** | **AI Service Failure:** If the external AI service is unavailable, the background task retries the job. If it fails repeatedly, the job is marked as failed, and the system logs an error. |
| **Postconditions** | The record's text is converted into vector embeddings, making it immediately available for semantic search and AI Q\&A features. |

Use Case M3-3.2: Monitor Embedding Jobs

| :---- | :---- |
| **Actors** | Staff / Admin |
| **Description** | Staff can view the status of embedding jobs (both the automated nightly runs and manual batches) to track progress and identify any processing errors. |
| **Preconditions** | The user has administrative or staff privileges. |
| **Main Flow** | Staff accesses the Embedding Jobs dashboard. The system displays a list of recent jobs along with their current status (e.g., queued, running, done, failed). |
| **Postconditions** | Staff can review progress and decide if any failed jobs need to be manually restarted. |

### ***Module 5: Hierarchical Submission Workflow***

This module covers the multi-stage institutional review pipeline that routes submitted records through the appropriate offices, including hierarchical routing logic per record type, parallel office clearance tracking with smart resubmission, PIN-gated record access for confidential viewing, document-level review and status transitions by staff, automated pipeline event notifications, and IP classification tagging for commercialization and community extension tracking.

#### **3.2.5.1 Document Routing and IP Evaluation Workflow**

FR-ID: FR-M5-01 

**Use Case Diagram**

![][image71]   

*Figure 61: Document Routing and IP Evaluation Workflow Use Case Diagram*

**Use Case Description**

Use Case M5-1: Document Routing and IP Evaluation Workflow

| Use Case | Document Routing and IP Evaluation Workflow |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Actors** | Student, Adviser, RDCO, ITSO, IERC, KTTO |
| **Description** | Record is in draft status; record type is set; required documents uploaded |
| **Preconditions** | The user is authenticated; RecordEmbedding rows exist; the third-party embedding API and LLM API are reachable. |
| **Main Flow(Proposal)** | Student submits → adviser\_review  Adviser checks document completeness Adviser approves → approved (visible as ongoing) OR declines → back to student for revision (loop) OR rejects → terminal When research is done, RDCO manually marks → completed (remains visible) |
| **Main Flow(Thesis/Research)** | Student submits → rdco\_intake RDCO checks completeness If complete → parallel\_review: IERC reviews Ethics Clearance \+ Release Form in parallel with KTTO reviewing Patent Search/Draft \+ IP Status \+ Pub/Conf \+ Commercialization Assessment All offices clear → rdco\_review → RDCO consolidates and approves → published |
| **Main Flow(Project)** | Student submits → rdco\_intake  RDCO checks completeness  If complete → itso\_review: ITSO reviews NDA \+ Assessment File; KTTO begins IP & Commercialization review in parallel from this stage  ITSO clears → IERC starts Ethics Clearance review; KTTO continues in parallel All three offices clear → rdco\_review → RDCO consolidates → published |
| **Main Flow(Proposal Completion)** | RDCO opens the Approved Proposals queue (/review/approved-proposals) RDCO sees all records with pipeline\_status \= "approved" (only Proposals can reach this status)  RDCO clicks "Mark as Completed" on the target row System calls POST /records/\<id\>/complete/, transitions record to completed  Row is removed from the queue; record owners are notified Record remains publicly visible with "Completed" badge |
| **Alternative Flow** | **Alternative Flow A:** RDCO returns submission for revision (incomplete) → declined; student uploads revised documents and resubmits. System validates that at least one new document version exists (uploaded after the most recent declined Review timestamp) before accepting the resubmission. All RecordClearance rows are deleted; record re-enters at rdco\_intake. **Alternative Flow B:** RDCO rejects at intake (out of scope, ineligible) → rejected terminal. **Alternative Flow C:** Any office (ITSO / IERC / KTTO) declines → declined; student uploads revised documents and resubmits. Smart clearance routing: the system inspects the stage field of the most recent declined Review. Only the declining office's RecordClearance row is reset to pending; all other offices' cleared status is preserved. The record re-enters at the correct stage: ITSO decline → itso\_review; IERC decline → parallel\_review; KTTO decline → itso\_review if ITSO is still pending, otherwise parallel\_review. The same new-document validation applies. **Alternative Flow D:** Any office (ITSO / IERC / KTTO) rejects (serious violation) → rejected terminal. **Alternative Flow E:** RDCO final issues revision → declined; student uploads revised documents and resubmits. All clearances are deleted; record re-enters at the first stage for its record type. **Alternative Flow F:** RDCO final rejects → rejected terminal. |
| **Postconditions** | Record status reflects current pipeline stage; transitions enforced server-side via RecordClearance rows for parallel stages; completed Proposals remain visible in Browse Collections |

### ***Module 6: Security and Authentication Design***

This module covers the system's security and access control layer, including JWT token enforcement and session lifecycle management, role-based permission checks on every protected endpoint, the role request and admin approval workflow, account locking and unlocking, active session monitoring and force-revocation, and data privacy consent recording with a tamper-evident audit log of all security-relevant events.

#### **3.2.6.1 JWT Authentication and Session Management**

FR-ID: FR-M6-01

**Use Case Diagram**

![][image87]     
*Figure 76: JWT Authentication and Session Management Use Case Diagram*

**Use Case Description**

Table M6-1: JWT Authentication and Session Management

| Use Case | Record IP Classification and Tagging |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Actors** | Authenticated User (primary), Unauthenticated Client, System |
| **Description** | The system enforces JWT-based authentication on every protected API endpoint. Short-lived access tokens (30 minutes) are validated on each request; when expired, the client silently obtains a new token pair using the stored refresh token. On logout, the refresh token is permanently blacklisted to prevent reuse. |
| **Preconditions** | JWT tokens issued at login via djangorestframework-simplejwt |
| **Main Flow** | Client includes JWT access token in Authorization: Bearer \<token\> header. DRF validates the token (signature, expiry — 30 minutes). If valid, request proceeds. When the access token expires, the client sends a refresh token to the refresh endpoint. The system validates the refresh token (not blacklisted, not expired). System issues a new access token. On logout, the client sends a refresh token to the blacklist endpoint. System blacklists the token via simplejwt's token blacklist. |
| **Alternative Flow** | **Access token expired or invalid:** HTTP 401; client should refresh.  **Refresh token blacklisted:** HTTP 401; user must log in again. |
| **Postconditions** | Only valid, non-blacklisted tokens grant access; logout is permanent for that refresh token. |

Table M6-2: Role-Based Access Control Enforcement

| Use Case | Role-Based Access Control Enforcement |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Actors** | All roles (primary), System |
| **Description** | Every API endpoint enforces server-side role-based permission checks. Each user's assigned role determines which actions they may perform: Student (submit/view own records), Adviser (review Proposals), KTTO (review IP/commercialization), RDCO (intake, final review, manage users), ITSO (review Projects), IERC (ethics review), Admin (all operations). Enforcement always occurs on the server regardless of what the frontend renders. |
| **Preconditions** | The user is authenticated; the role is assigned to the user account. |
| **Main Flow** | An authenticated user sends a request to any API endpoint. DRF permission class checks the user's assigned role against the endpoint's required permission. If the role is permitted, the request proceeds. Role checks are enforced server-side regardless of what the frontend renders. |
| **Alternative Flow** | **Role not permitted:** HTTP 403 Forbidden.  **No role assigned:** Treated as lowest-privilege; most actions blocked. |
| **Postconditions** | Only permitted actions succeed; all permission checks are server-side. |

The affected user's next request returns HTTP 401\. |
| **Alternative Flow** | **JTI not found:** HTTP 404 "Session not found." |
| **Postconditions** | Token blacklisted; user forced to re-authenticate; revocation recorded in audit log. |

| **Postconditions** | Consent recorded; all security events in the immutable audit trail; only Django Admin can read the log. |

### ***Module 7: KPI Dashboard & Analytics***

This module provides institutional stakeholders with real-time visibility into the state of the research submission pipeline and aggregate reporting tools for strategic decision-making. It delivers role-differentiated dashboard views that surface each user's relevant queue, processing time metrics, and status counts — ensuring that staff officers, faculty advisers, and RDCO administrators can monitor their responsibilities at a glance without querying the system manually. A report generation feature complements the dashboard by allowing authorized staff to produce filtered summary reports of institutional research output, exportable as structured spreadsheets for use in governance submissions, accreditation documentation, and IP portfolio reviews.

| Use Case | Embedding Index Management |

Admin can trigger a full re-index of all records (re-embed every record using the current embedding model), or trigger a targeted re-embed for a single record. All embedding operations run asynchronously via Celery and are tracked as EmbeddingJob rows. |
| **Preconditions** | Admin is authenticated with is\_staff \= True. |

The task iterates all published records and calls embed\_record.delay(record\_id) for each. Job progress is visible in the Embedding Job Log. |
| **Main Flow (Re-embed Single Record)** | Admin enters a record ID and clicks "Embed Record." The system calls POST /ai/embed/\<pk\>/ which enqueues embed\_record.delay(record\_id) for that record. |
| **Main Flow (View Job Log)** | Admin sees the Embedding Job Log below the index status. Each row shows: record title, embedding status (pending / in\_progress / done / failed), model name, and timestamp. Admin can filter by status. |
| **Alternative Flow** | **No published records:** System shows "No records to index."  **Job already running:** If a full re-index is already in progress, the system returns a message "Re-index already running. Check the job log for progress." |
| **Postconditions** | Embedding jobs are queued and will be processed by Celery workers. The job log updates as each job completes. |

## ***3.3 Non-functional requirements***

### ***Performance***

**NFR-P1 \- Concurrent User Support**  
The ***system shall*** support a minimum of 100 simultaneous authenticated user sessions without performance degradation, with an average response time not exceeding 2 seconds and zero session failures under this load. *Validation:* Apache JMeter load test at two tiers: (1) MVP Baseline \- 100 virtual users, 30-minute continuous duration, ramp-up over 5 minutes, verifying zero crashes and sub-2-second average response throughout; (2) Enterprise-phase stress test \- 1,000 virtual users under the same conditions, measuring degradation profile and identifying the failure threshold.

**NFR-P2 \- Page Load Response Time**  
The ***system shall*** deliver page responses within 2 seconds for the 95th percentile of all HTTP requests under normal operating load of 100 or fewer concurrent users. *Validation*: JMeter response time percentile report generated from a representative load test covering all core page routes including the student portal, role dashboards, document upload interface, and the RDCO KPI dashboard. 

**NFR-P3 \- Chatbot Query Response Time**  
The ***IRIS RAG chatbot shall*** return a complete response within 3 seconds for the 95th percentile of all user queries submitted under normal operating load. *Validation*: automated query timing test sending 20 consecutive representative natural language queries against the deployed RAG pipeline and measuring the 95th percentile response time across all queries. 

**NFR-P4 \- PDF Automatic Indexing Time**  
The ***system shall*** complete full-text extraction, keyword tagging, and vector embedding for a standard 10-page, 10MB research PDF within 30 seconds of upload confirmation. *Validation*: timed integration test uploading 5 representative sample research papers of approximately 10MB each and verifying all complete within the 30-second threshold. 

**NFR-P5 \- Maximum Upload Payload Size**  
The ***system shall*** reject any document upload exceeding a file size of 50MB at the gateway level (NGINX/Django). *Validation*: attempt to upload a 51MB PDF; verify that the system returns an HTTP 413 Payload Too Large error.

### ***Security***

**NFR-S1 \- Encryption at Rest**  
***All sensitive IRIS database fields*** including the PostgreSQL data directory and uploaded PDF file storage \- ***shall be*** protected by disk-level or filesystem-level encryption. *Validation:* confirmation that the server's storage volumes are mounted with encryption enabled, verifying that raw disk access without the OS-level decryption passphrase does not expose readable data

**NFR-S2 \- Session Expiry and Re-Authentication**  
***IRIS user sessions shall*** expire automatically after 30 consecutive minutes of inactivity, upon which the server-side JWT token shall be invalidated and the user redirected to the login page requiring full re-authentication. *Validation*: automated idle-timeout test \- authenticate, wait 31 minutes, attempt a protected API call, and verify an HTTP 401 response is returned and the token rejected on all subsequent requests.

**NFR-S3 \- Encrypted Data Transmission**  
***All data transmitted between IRIS client applications and the server shall*** use HTTPS secured by TLS 1.2 or higher, and any HTTP request received on port 80 shall be automatically redirected to HTTPS with a 301 status code. *Validation*: confirm that the IRIS deployment URL is accessible via HTTPS and that HTTP requests on port 80 redirect to HTTPS. Certificate validity confirmed via browser padlock indicator.

**NFR-S4 \- Role Boundary Enforcement**  
The ***system shall*** enforce role boundaries such that no authenticated user can view, modify, approve, or export records belonging to a workflow tier above their assigned role, with permissions enforced server-side on every API call independent of client-side UI state. *Validation*: boundary test using a Student-role account to attempt direct API calls to RDCO-restricted endpoints, verifying all such requests return HTTP 403 Forbidden with no restricted data in any response body. 

**NFR-S5 \- Audit Log Retention and Immutability**  
***System audit logs shall be*** retained for a minimum of 12 months from the date of each recorded event and shall be immutable \- no user role, including System Administrators, shall be able to edit or delete log entries through any exposed interface. *Validation*: attempt to DELETE a log record via both the REST API and the Django admin panel using a System Administrator account, verifying both are rejected at the data layer. 

**NFR-S6 \- Brute-Force Login Protection**  
***The system shall use django-axes*** to detect and block repeated failed login attempts. After a configurable number of consecutive failures (default: 3\) within a configurable time window (default: 10 minutes), the account or source IP shall be locked and further login attempts rejected with HTTP 403\. Lock events shall be written to the audit log. Staff administrators shall be able to unlock affected accounts via the account management interface. *Validation:* automated test submitting 6 consecutive failed login attempts for a single account within the configured window, verifying the 6th attempt returns HTTP 403, the account appears as locked in the admin interface, and a lock event is recorded in the audit log.

### 

### 

### ***Reliability***

**NFR-R1 \- System Uptime**   
The ***system shall*** maintain a minimum uptime of 99.5% measured on a calendar-month basis, excluding pre-announced maintenance windows not exceeding 4 hours per calendar month, equating to a maximum of approximately 3.6 hours of allowable unplanned downtime per month. *Validation*: uptime monitoring tool deployed against the IRIS production URL throughout one full academic semester, generating monthly uptime reports with all unplanned downtime events logged by timestamp, duration, and root cause. 

**NFR-R2 \- Failure Recovery Time**   
Following an unexpected failure \- including server crash, power loss, or fatal application error \- the ***system shall*** automatically restore to its last known stable operational state within 5 minutes with no loss of committed data transactions. *Validation*: forced server restart under active load, measuring elapsed time to first successful authenticated request and verifying all pre-restart committed records remain intact. 

**NFR-R3 \- Data Integrity Under Concurrency**   
The ***system shall*** maintain full data integrity under concurrent write operations, with no partial, duplicate, or corrupted records resulting from simultaneous PDF submissions by multiple users. *Validation*: JMeter concurrent write test with 50 virtual users simultaneously submitting PDF uploads, verifying the resulting record count exactly matches the number of successful upload responses with no duplicates or missing fields. 

**NFR-R4 \-- Data Backup and Recovery Point Objective**  
The PostgreSQL database and on-premise file storage shall be backed up via automated daily snapshots. The Recovery Point Objective (RPO) shall not exceed 24 hours, meaning no more than one day of committed data may be lost in the event of an unrecoverable failure. Backup integrity shall be verified monthly via a test restoration to a staging environment. *Validation:* review of the backup schedule configuration confirming daily execution; restoration drill performed on a staging instance using the most recent backup, verifying all records and uploaded files are intact.

### ***Usability***

**NFR-U1 \- SUS Score Target**   
The ***system shall*** achieve a minimum mean SUS score of 75, corresponding to a "Good" usability rating, as measured by a representative survey of CIT-U IRIS users across at least three role groups administered within two weeks of deployment. *Validation*: post-deployment administration of the standard 10-question SUS questionnaire included in Appendix B, with a mean score across all respondents meeting or exceeding 75\.

**NFR-U2 \- Submission Time After Training**   
A ***first-time IRIS user***, following a 1-hour onboarding session, ***shall be*** able to complete a full IP disclosure submission including PDF upload and consent acknowledgment within 10 minutes without external assistance. *Validation*: timed usability test with a minimum of 5 student participants who have no prior IRIS experience, each completing the submission task independently after the onboarding session, with all 5 finishing within the 10-minute threshold. 

**NFR-U3 \- Mobile Responsiveness**   
***All IRIS core user workflows \-*** including login, IP disclosure submission, RAG chatbot query, and workflow status view \- ***shall be*** fully functional and usable on viewport widths of 360px and above without horizontal scrolling, targeting common budget Android devices in the Philippine market. *Validation*: cross-device test using Chrome DevTools emulation at 360px combined with a physical test on a 360px-width Android device, confirming all core workflows complete with no horizontal scroll, overlapping elements, or broken components. 

### ***Maintainability***

**NFR-M1 \- Django MVT Architectural Pattern**   
***All IRIS backend features shall be*** implemented following a layered Django architecture consistent with the API-first design approach. Business logic shall reside in model methods and dedicated service modules only. Django views shall function exclusively as API endpoint handler, with no business logic or direct query construction embedded in view functions. The Django Template layer is not used for client-facing rendering, as all UI is served by the React SPA frontend. *Validation:* code architecture review prior to each sprint release verifying that (1) view functions contain no business logic beyond request validation and serializer invocation, (2) all business rules are encapsulated in model methods or dedicated service modules, and (3) no Django template files exist in production application directories

**NFR-M2 \- Inline Documentation**   
***All Python functions exceeding 10 lines of code or containing conditional branching logic shall*** include a docstring specifying purpose, parameters (name, type, and description), return value (type and description), and exceptions raised. *Validation*: automated docstring coverage check using `pydocstyle` run in the GitHub Actions CI pipeline on every pull request, blocking any merge where a qualifying function is missing a compliant docstring. 

**NFR-M3 \- Modular Architecture**   
***The IRIS system architecture shall*** allow new feature modules to be integrated without modifying existing module source code, with new modules registered exclusively via Django's app configuration mechanism. *Validation*: architecture review confirming a new feature can be added as a separate Django app with all integration points \- URL routing, signal connections, and database migrations \- self-contained within the new app's directory and registered only through `INSTALLED_APPS`.
